title: handsets.toml — the hardware inventory
description: The phone plant: what physically exists. `doorman render` generates the per-handset Asterisk config from this file, so ids, endpoints, and dialplan cannot drift apart. Changes when you buy hardware. Rules live in policy.toml.

groups.description: Named sets of handsets, usable anywhere a handset id is.

x-rules: May not collide with any handset id.
Must be unique.

handsets.description: Every physical phone or dialplan destination.

email.description: Where this phone's mailbox mails its messages, with the recording attached (voicemail.conf's attach=yes). Optional; the address on the generated mailbox line. Needs mailbox.
x-rules: Needs mailbox on the same handset.
When several phones share a box, the first address given is the box's.

endpoint.description: Asterisk endpoint. Must be PJSIP/<id> — `doorman render` enforces the match so the generated config cannot disagree with the inventory.

x-rules: Must be unique across handsets and groups.

label.description: Human name, shown in `doorman check` output.

mac.description: The phone's hardware address, from the sticker under the battery or on the box. Any written form is accepted — aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff, AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF, aabbccddeeff — and normalised. With model, it lets `doorman render` write the phone's own configuration file and `doorman provision` hand it over, which is what turns adding a phone into two touches instead of a web form.
x-rules: Two handsets may not share a MAC.
mac and model travel together: set both or neither.

mailbox.description: This phone's own voicemail box. `doorman render` writes it into voicemail_handsets.conf when VOICEMAIL_<BOX>_PIN is in .env (a box without one is assumed hand-written in voicemail.conf, which is every box from before render made them); a call to this phone's number that rings out — or finds it busy — lands in it; the phone's voicemail key (*97) opens it without asking which or for a PIN; and its message-waiting lamp follows it. Two phones may name one box and share it. A policy file's `voicemail = "…"` may name it too, so a stranger with this room's PIN who rings out leaves the message on this room's phone.
x-rules: `doorman rotate --voicemail [box …]` sets or rotates the PINs; `doorman init` gives every room its own box.
`doorman check` lists every box handsets name and every box policy sends callers to, and says which the tool writes.

model.description: Which provisioning template the phone gets. `doorman provision --models` lists the known ids (grandstream-wp826, grandstream-grp2601p, …); `doorman check` refuses an unknown one with a suggestion.
x-rules: mac and model travel together: set both or neither.
A known model without a template yet is accepted; `doorman render` says so and the phone keeps the manual path.

number.description: Internal extension for handset-to-handset dialling and BLF hints. 0 or absent means not directly dialable.
x-rules: Two handsets may not share a number.
0 is allowed and means not dialable.

page.description: Include in the page-all group reached by dialling 500.

password_env.description: Name of the .env variable holding this handset's SIP password. The secret itself never appears in this file. `doorman render` substitutes it and fails if unset.
x-rules: Required by `doorman render`, which reports it as an error when missing.
Names a variable; never put the password here.

phonebook.description: Which directories this phone shows: "house" (every handset with a number and the feature codes), "people" (policy.toml's [[people]]), or a contacts.toml source id — a whole address book, which is why it is opt-in per phone. Absent means house and people. A child's phone might be just ["house"].
x-rules: Entries may not repeat.
A contacts.toml source id is checked by `doorman check` against that file; the loader only checks the shape.
At least one [[handsets]] entry is required.
A group id may appear anywhere a handset id may, and expands at load time.
Groups may contain handsets only, never other groups — no cycles.
